advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the added JIRA_USER-email and empty-query_project fail-close checks on the runtime scope path are the intended AC4 delta (they are stricter than legacy assert_env_ready) and are documented as such.
evidence: runtime.py assert_cloud_scope_ready calls `_assert_cloud_user_is_email(scope.user)` and raises on empty `scope.query_project`
Legacy Cloud assert_env_ready (backend.py:227-243) only checks presence of JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN — no email-format or empty-project check
backend.py:222-226 routes to assert_cloud_scope_ready when `self._scope is not None`
advisory.finding: The runtime scope-readiness path (assert_cloud_scope_ready) enforces two checks the legacy ambient assert_env_ready did NOT: JIRA_USER must be an email, and query_project must be non-empty. A JiraBackend composed via the runtime therefore rejects configs (non-email user, empty project) that the legacy ambient-resolution path accepted — a behavior change on the new binding path.

evidence: search_files for 'assert_datacenter_scope_ready' in tests returns (no matches)

DC held-out test test_datacenter_scope_survives_poisoned_ambient_after_compose supplies reconciler.base_url and env JIRA_PAT is present via _default_jira_env (only JIRA_API_TOKEN cleared in cloud tests)
AC4 docstring: DC readiness 'raises BackendEnvError when a DC connection essential (the base url / the env-only JIRA_PAT) is missing — before the real client is built'
advisory.finding: The Data Center fail-closed readiness contract (assert_datacenter_scope_ready) is untested: no test composes a DC runtime with a missing base_url or a missing JIRA_PAT and asserts a typed BackendEnvError before the real client is built. All DC tests supply a valid base_url and PAT, so the missing-essential branch (runtime.py:384-396) and the DC scope branch of JiraDataCenterBackend.assert_env_ready never execute.
scenarios: Operator runs DC reconcile with reconciler.base_url unset or JIRA_PAT unset — regression that silently builds a client or raises a bare error would not be caught

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Call assert_datacenter_scope_ready(s) in ReconcilerRuntime._build_datacenter before constructing the transport, mirroring the Cloud path, so an empty base_url fails closed at build.
evidence: runtime.py:_build_cloud: `assert_cloud_scope_ready(s)` is called before `transport = acli.AcliClient(...)` (fail-closed at build)
runtime.py:_build_datacenter (lines 163-173): builds `_LazyDataCenterClient(self.auth, s)` and `JiraDataCenterTransport(...)` with NO call to `assert_datacenter_scope_ready(s)`

transport.py:150-194 build_client_from_settings: the only fail-closed guard is `if not (settings.pat or "").strip(): raise BackendEnvError(...)` — empty `settings.url` is passed to `jira_cls(server=settings.url, ...)` unchecked

assert_datacenter_scope_ready (runtime.py:375-396) validates `base_url` presence + `JIRA_PAT`, but is only reached from JiraDataCenterBackend.assert_env_ready (backend.py:408), not from the DC build path — so a caller that builds and uses the backend without calling assert_env_ready never validates base_url
advisory.finding: DC build path does not fail closed on a missing/empty base_url at build time, unlike the Cloud path. ReconcilerRuntime._build_cloud calls assert_cloud_scope_ready(s) before constructing the transport, but _build_datacenter constructs the backend (with a lazy client) WITHOUT calling assert_datacenter_scope_ready. The only build-deferred DC guard, build_client_from_settings, checks solely settings.pat — an empty base_url with a present JIRA_PAT would construct jira.JIRA(server='') rather than raising the typed BackendEnvError before I/O.
scenarios: DC backend selected with JIRA_PAT set but reconciler.base_url unset/empty; a code path that reaches the transport without first calling backend.assert_env_ready constructs a client against an empty server URL instead of failing closed with the typed BackendEnvError
advisory.suggested_fix: In _build_datacenter, add `assert_datacenter_scope_ready(s)` at the top of the real-transport branch (before building _LazyDataCenterClient / JiraDataCenterTransport), parallel to _build_cloud's assert_cloud_scope_ready(s).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Either thread the captured comment_max_chars/jira_cli_timeout into the built transport/backend, or drop them from ReconcilerSettings if this stage does not yet consume them.
evidence: search for `_scope.comment_max_chars` and `_scope.jira_cli_timeout` returned (no matches) — no consumer reads them from the scope

acli.py:250-270 AcliClient._run delegates to acli_subprocess._run_acli which resolves the timeout from ambient config (acli_subprocess.py:86 `load_config().reconciler.jira_cli_timeout`), not from the captured scope
dropped.finding: ReconcilerSettings captures comment_max_chars and jira_cli_timeout at compose time, but neither the JiraBackend nor JiraDataCenterBackend nor the AcliClient built in _build_cloud reads them from the scope; the acli timeout is still re-resolved from ambient config at call time, so the 'compose once, no ambient re-resolution' guarantee does not hold for these fields.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the mutation test to expect the specific frozen-dataclass exception (dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError / AttributeError) rather than including bare Exception.
evidence: test_operation_bindings_runtime.py:82: 'with pytest.raises((AttributeError, TypeError, Exception)):' — Exception is a superclass of AttributeError/TypeError and of most errors
frozen dataclass assignment raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError (a subclass of AttributeError)
dropped.finding: The frozen-settings mutation test asserts too little: pytest.raises((AttributeError, TypeError, Exception)) includes bare Exception, which matches virtually any error, so the test would pass even if the assignment failed for an unrelated reason (or if a different exception type were raised) — it does not pin the frozen-dataclass contract.
scenarios: The dataclass is silently made non-frozen but an unrelated attribute error path still raises during teardown/other logic
dropped.suggested_fix: Use `with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):` (or AttributeError) instead of the tuple that includes Exception.
